pages.text: The $(item)MoE routing rack$() is the $(bold)central deployment hub$() of the open camp: insert the $(item)open-weight module$() a pretraining run produced and the model becomes resident in cluster memory, routed from one place for every downstream consumer.$(br2)It bills no Tokens — the open camp's compute is your own machine room.

pages.title: The 5×5×5 stepped structure
pages.text: $(li)$(#0E7490)y=0$(): the heavy $(item)computer casing$() base plate; energy, item and maintenance hatches all ride this layer.$(li)$(#0E7490)y=1$(): the deployment console row. The controller sits front-centre at $(bold)(2, 1, 0)$(); the deployment slot and the four LoRA slots are on its screen.$(li)$(#0E7490)y=2$(): the routing core — $(item)cleanroom glass$() around the $(item)advanced computer casing$() compute spine.$(li)$(#0E7490)y=3$(): the re-widened shoulder; $(bold)y=4$() steps in one block as the roof heat ring.

pages.title: Model identity: whichever module is inserted is deployed
pages.text: The module's $(bold)hc_model_id$() decides which model is deployed:$(li)All five open models $(bold)deploy independently$(); each one asks the pool for its own declared VRAM and bills its own CWU/t.$(li)A very old module without that field $(bold)reads as Qwen 9187$() and does not become junk.$(br2)Swap the module and only that model's cost applies — nothing bleeds into another family.

pages.title: Loading, OOM and eviction
pages.text: Once weights are inserted the router asks the cluster memory pool for the TB the model declares:$(li)Pool big enough → $(bold)ONLINE$(); the model is resident and $(bold)really draws its own CWU/t every tick$() (DeepSeek draws only 25%).$(li)Pool too small → $(bold)OOM$(): the load is $(bold)refused$() and no compute is billed.$(br2)$(bold)Pulling the card, pulling a HBM module, cutting a memory cabinet's power or a chunk reload$() takes the model offline on the very next tick (EVICTED/EMPTY), and every projection it cast on the inference hatches is withdrawn with it.

pages.title: LoRA extensions & DeepThink
pages.text: $(bold)LoRA extensions$(): a model with four slots (Qwen 9187) takes the 0.2.1 $(item)mining LoRA card$() or $(item)chemical LoRA card$() at $(bold)+4 TB / +4 CWU/t$() each. The router $(bold)projects the specialisation onto the inference hatches within 16 blocks$(): that domain's chanced by-product gains 1/3 per card (1/3 → 2/3 → 100%).$(br2)$(bold)DeepThink$(): DeepSeek-V6767 Pro reserves $(bold)+16 TB$() while charged and forces the linked hatches' chanced by-products to $(bold)100%$().$(br2)Either can push the job out of the pool, so buy the TB before switching them on.

pages.title: Cloned copies
pages.text: An open master weight can be cloned cheaply in the $(item)HV micro burner$(): $(bold)1 open-weight module ($(bold)not consumed — the original stays$()) + 1 $(item)blank carrier$() + 600 EU/t for 200 ticks$() yields one copy carrying $(bold)a complete duplicate$() of $()hc_model_id / hc_domain / hc_precision / hc_version$(). A second machine room does not need to re-run the 2400-tick training.
